samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2023-10-29 to 2024-01-14. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Amazon launched its first two prototype satellites, Kuipersat-1 and Kuipersat-2, for its Project Kuiper internet constellation on October 6, 2023. The mission, named Protoflight, was successfully carried out by a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Atlas V rocket that lifted off from Space Launch Complex-41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. This launch marked Amazon's initial step into space to test its satellite technology before commencing full-scale production launches. The broader objective of Project Kuiper is to establish a mega-constellation of over 3,200 satellites in low Earth orbit to provide high-speed broadband internet to unserved and underserved communities globally, positioning itself as a competitor to services like SpaceX's Starlink. Following the successful test mission, both prototype satellites were set to be actively deorbited. <2> On Friday, September 29, 2023, at 10:00 PM EDT, SpaceX successfully launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 22 Starlink satellites (designated as Group 6-19) to low-Earth orbit. [2, 4, 5] The mission lifted off from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. [2, 4] Following stage separation, the Falcon 9's first stage booster landed on the 'A Shortfall of Gravitas' droneship in the Atlantic Ocean. [5] This was the tenth flight for this particular first-stage booster. [4, 5] <3> On September 19, 2023, Rocket Lab's 41st Electron rocket mission, dubbed "We Will Never Desert You," experienced a significant failure, resulting in the loss of the payload. The rocket launched from Rocket Lab's complex in Mahia, New Zealand, at 6:55 p.m. local time (2:55 a.m. EDT). The payload was a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) Earth-observation satellite, known as Acadia-2, for the California-based company Capella Space. The mission proceeded as planned through the first stage burn and stage separation. However, an anomaly occurred approximately two and a half minutes into the flight, shortly after the scheduled ignition of the second stage engine, leading to the end of the mission. Subsequent investigation identified the likely cause as an electrical arc within the power supply system for the upper stage. The failure broke a streak of 19 successful launches for the company. <4> ABL Space Systems has been awarded a $15 million contract by the U.S. Space Systems Command (SSC) to execute a tactically responsive space (TacRS) launch demonstration. The contract, part of an existing Strategic Funding Initiative (STRATFI), was awarded by the Assured Access to Space office to support TacRS initiatives aimed at rapidly deploying assets to orbit for urgent military needs. Under the contract, ABL will prepare to launch its RS1 vehicle from one of two potential sites on short notice from the Space Force, with the mission planned for execution within the next two years. This effort is designed to demonstrate the flexibility required for a persistent, rapid-response launch capability. <5> On September 17, 2023, startup Stoke Space announced it had successfully conducted a vertical takeoff and vertical landing (VTVL) test of its reusable second-stage prototype, known as "Hopper2". The developmental flight test took place at the company's facility in Moses Lake, Washington, where the vehicle flew to an altitude of 30 feet for 15 seconds before landing in its designated zone. The test was a crucial milestone, successfully demonstrating the viability of several of the company's innovative technologies, including its novel hydrogen/oxygen engine, a regeneratively cooled heat shield, and its differential throttle thrust vector control system. According to Stoke Space, this was the final test in the Hopper technology demonstration program, providing a large amount of data to help evolve the design from a demonstrator to a reliable, reusable space vehicle. <6> Firefly Aerospace successfully launched the VICTUS NOX mission for the U.S. Space Force from Space Launch Complex 2 (SLC-2) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California. [1] The mission, whose name is Latin for 'conquer the night', was designed to demonstrate a tactically responsive space capability. [5] A new record was set for responsive launch, with the Firefly Alpha rocket lifting off just 27 hours after receiving the official order from the military. [5, 7] The launch vehicle carried a satellite built by Millennium Space Systems, which will be used for a Space Domain Awareness (SDA) mission. [1, 5] The entire process, from a 'hot standby' phase to payload integration and launch, was part of an end-to-end demonstration to prove the United States can rapidly place an asset into orbit with little notice to augment its space capabilities in response to a threat. [1, 5] <7> A United Launch Alliance (ULA) Atlas V rocket successfully launched the SILENTBARKER/NROL-107 mission on September 10, 2023, from Space Launch Complex-41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida. This classified mission is a joint initiative between the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) and the U.S. Space Force's Space Systems Command (SSC). Its purpose is to enhance Space Domain Awareness by using a space-based sensor to search for, detect, and track objects to provide timely threat intelligence. The mission, which had been delayed from its original August 29 date due to Tropical Storm Idalia, involves multiple satellites that will operate in a near-geosynchronous orbit. The satellites are expected to become fully operational by 2026. This launch marked the 157th mission for ULA and the final NRO mission to launch aboard an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral. <8> On September 2, 2023, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket successfully launched 13 satellites for the U.S. Space Force's Space Development Agency (SDA) from Vandenberg Space Force Base, California. [2, 5] This mission was the second launch for the SDA's Tranche 0 demonstration group, part of the Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture, a layered network designed for global military communication and missile tracking. [4, 7] The payload included 10 data transport satellites from Lockheed Martin, one from York Space Systems, and two missile-tracking satellites from SpaceX. [7] The launch occurred at 7:26 a.m. local time after being delayed from August 31 and September 1. [2, 7] <9> Virgin Galactic's third commercial spaceflight, 'Galactic 03,' successfully flew three private astronauts to the edge of space on September 8, 2023, from Spaceport America in New Mexico. The flight was the company's fourth successful spaceflight in four months. The passengers were designated as the first of Virgin Galactic's 'Founder' astronauts, having purchased their tickets as early as 2005. The crew included American Ken Baxter (Astronaut 014), Timothy Nash from South Africa (Astronaut 015), and Adrian Reynard from the United Kingdom (Astronaut 016). Baxter, a Las Vegas real estate investor, reportedly bought his ticket in 2004 after seeing a segment on the X Prize. The VSS Unity spacecraft, piloted by Commander Nicola Pecile and Pilot Michael Masucci, reached an apogee of 55 miles (88.56 km) and a top speed of Mach 2.95. The mission was announced on August 28, 2023, with the flight window set to open on September 8, 2023.
